report.source_text: Molecular testing of the coding fragment of the ZEB2 gene (exon fragment from amino acid position His655 to Ser840) detected a mutation of p.Gla694Ter in one allele. The above mutation involves a C nucleotide substitution at T at position c.2080, resulting in a change in the amino acid Gln to the STOP codon at position 694 of the amino acid chain, which ultimately leads to premature termination of translation.

report.source_text: The patient did not acquire the ability to speak and, therefore, the visual acuity (VA) could not be verified. The eyeballs remained in alternating convergent strabismus, Hirschberg test 15–20°, no limitation in eye movements was detected (Figure 2).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 9-year-old girl, suspected of having Mowat-Wilson syndrome, was referred for ophthalmological evaluation. Genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis by identifying a p.Gln694Ter mutation in the ZEB2 gene. Initial ophthalmological examination revealed alternating convergent strabismus, normal pupillary responses, pallor of the temporal optic nerve discs, subtle inferior elevation of the optic disc in the right eye, and significant astigmatism in both eyes. Ocular ultrasound suggested optic nerve drusen. Less than a year later, the patient's mother reported a worsening interest in her surroundings, and it was noted that the patient's right eye no longer followed objects, while the left eye continued to do so.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Diagnosis of Mowat-Wilson syndrome confirmed by p.Gln694Ter mutation in the ZEB2 gene.
Ophthalmological examination revealed alternating convergent strabismus.
Ophthalmological examination showed pallor of the optic nerve discs on the temporal side and subtle inferior elevation of the optic disc in the right eye.
Cycloplegic autorefraction confirmed significant astigmatism in both eyes (RE: -0.5 Dsph -6.0 Dcyl ax 178°, LE: -1.0 Dsph -6.5 Dcyl ax 162°).
Ocular ultrasound showed increased echogenicity in the optic disc area, consistent with optic nerve drusen.
Clinical progression noted worsening interest in surroundings and the right eye not following objects less than a year after initial presentation.
